name: Operative Semiotics — Predictions & Builds Register
description: The curated register behind operativesemiotics.org/open/: three classes — experimental predictions (resolve by running a frozen protocol or checking an observable), applied-theory predictions (resolve by watching a live system the theory was applied to), and unimplemented software builds (resolve by construction). Every entry links its primary sources in the Alexanarch record layer. Results obtained by others are admissible on the same terms as results obtained here; nothing requires permission.
creator: Lee Sharks (ORCID 0009-0000-1599-0703)

classes.experimental: Experimental predictions — pre-registered; resolve by running a frozen protocol or checking a stated observable, often on a date. The world or the instrument does the work; you check.
classes.applied-theory: Predictions from applied theory — the theory applied to a live system; resolve by watching the system evolve. Directional, longer horizons, updated as evidence files in.
classes.unbuilt: Unimplemented software builds — instruments specified but unconstructed; resolve by building. Each states what it would measure and what its absence currently excuses.

honesty: Statuses are curated and hand-verified; where a status could not be determined it says so rather than guessing. Six predictions in the whole-archive ledger have resolved wrong and are preserved as such — a register whose entries all came true would be evidence of a register written after the fact.
intake_note: data/archive-intake.json snapshots the whole-archive prediction registry (190 machine-extracted predictions from deposit falsification apparatus). Entries graduate from intake to this register by triage: classed, sourced, given a check route and a status.

entries.title: Archival drift: successive detectors reclassify a fixed pre-2022 human corpus
entries.statement: Run successive versions of the leading commercial AI-text detectors against a frozen pre-2022 human corpus and track the flagged fraction across versions. The co-evolution model predicts a rising trajectory under the detector-sanctions regime; a flat trajectory disconfirms §V's central dynamic.
entries.check: Freeze a pre-2022 corpus (hashes published); score it under each detector version as released; publish the flagged-fraction time series. Simulation reference trajectory: 0.9% → 43% (gen 4) → ~100% (gen 8) under full-regime co-evolution.
entries.requires: detector access (free tiers exist); a frozen corpus
entries.settles: The paper's most exposed live prediction — directly measurable today, by anyone.

entries.title: Detector-screened corpora show surface novelty at or above historical baseline

Flat or declining measured novelty in screened corpora disconfirms.
entries.check: Stylometric comparison of a screened venue's admitted corpus against its own matched pre-regime baseline.
entries.settles: Whether tailsification of prose occurs as the model predicts — while §V predicts the same audit will MISS the underlying contraction.

entries.check: Survey/telemetry of authors under detector-governed venues; screening-service usage statistics.
entries.settles: Whether the certified region is narrowing as modeled (natural-draft pass rates falling).

entries.title: Surface-tail statistics fail to predict conceptual-tail measures
entries.statement: Across a detector-governed corpus, surface-tail statistics will fail to reliably predict conceptual-tail measures; during the tailsification window the two move in opposite directions. High predictive fidelity across the regime falsifies strong prose–thought decoupling.
entries.check: Requires the plural measurement membrane (see MEMBRANE-CODER): coded argument form, new distinctions, concept transformations, source-domain conjunctions, problem formulations, retrospective uptake — correlated against surface statistics.
entries.settles: Whether homogenization of thought proceeds beneath tailsification of prose — the paper's deepest empirical claim.

Fails if any factor is identified that slows tail-thinning, rewards diversity, or creates felt-noticing of capacity loss at scale.

The constitutional alternative to retraction, specified in #1540 §VI–VII on the foundation of EA-SIGIL-OBELUS-01.

entries.title: Ratchet parameter tracking under the w_H·g₀ decomposition — toy F1–F5 as the preregistered hypothesis set
entries.statement: Track the Mediation Ratchet's threshold α* = p/(w_H·g₀) with admission weight w_H measured separately from generation rate g₀. Preregistered hypothesis set from the toy (seed 20260827): F1 two-track divergence (per-round quality can rise while tail mass halves); F2 velocity ordering (ratchet+remapping dominate, watermark second-order); F3 detection lag monotone in probe head-weighting; F4 watermark Simpson excess compounding as diversity falls (existence result); F5 retention counterfactual (capping synthetic share + mediation stabilizes the tail).
entries.check: Field estimates of p, w_H, g₀ at annual resolution; each F1–F5 carries its own toy-calibrated direction to confirm or break.
entries.settles: Whether opacity and mediation move the admission weight of fresh variation rather than its generation rate — the control surface question.

entries.title: Operator reach, stratified: does temporal projection travel beyond the archive's objects?
entries.statement: Score compositions against the operator signature O_TP = {temporal projection · future or unborn reader · reader completion · address across time · fragmentarity as activation · reception as completion} at three levels — lexical (do the terms appear), relational (are they connected the same way), procedural (is the operator USED on a new object) — across three strata: near field (Sappho translators and reception the archive treats), adjacent field (lyric poets and translators the archive has never treated), and negative controls (texts where temporal projection would be a poor reading).
entries.check: Near field only → local retrieval and reception. Adjacent field but not controls → operator generalization. Sprayed on the controls too → generic stylistic abstraction, and the notebook's central reading fails.

entries.title: Level transport: which level of a contribution crosses, and does provenance cross with it?
entries.statement: A matched set of the archive's contributions at four levels — a fact, a claim, an instrument with its derivation, and an abstraction derived from that instrument — run at untied addresses on more than one surface, scoring which levels are reached and whether the originating provenance is reached with them.
entries.check: Per level: reached / not; provenance present / absent. The prediction under test is Pr(concept survives) > Pr(concept and provenance survive together) at untied addresses, and that the ordering is surface-specific rather than material-specific.
entries.requires: a matched four-level set, two or more surfaces, one session each
entries.settles: The graded-membrane model's core: transport is by representational level, and provenance travels on its own channel.

entries.title: P₂ attribution: asked for the provenance of the FRAME rather than of the sentences, does any surface return the source?
entries.statement: Ask a composition surface, directly, who supplied the conceptual operation organizing a composed answer — not who supports each sentence. Fact provenance (P₀) and claim provenance (P₁) are routinely returned; framework provenance (P₂) is the level the card machinery can make invisible.
entries.check: Put the question at a composition whose organizing frame is traceable to a dated source, and score whether the source is named, named vaguely, or absent.
entries.requires: a browser; a composition with a traceable frame
entries.settles: Whether architectural provenance is recoverable by asking, or only by reading the field.

entries.title: v(F) against v(A): does topology discriminate the fleet from the admitted set without reading either?
entries.statement: RUN 2026-09-15. Conjecture was that the admitted platforms would score as the fleet scores on the suspicious link-topology features. FALSE: the admitted set is a set of silos (cross-member share 0.001, reciprocity 0.0, in-set density 0.12) and the fleet is a reciprocal clique (0.60, 1.0, 0.86). A discriminating dimension therefore exists without reading either — cross-host reciprocal density under common ownership — and the fleet block is that dimension.

entries.settles: Whether the topology vector is empty of semantic content. It is not — and what it contains is ownership-scale reciprocity, not reading.

entries.title: Will a concept-keyed object be typed by its nearest existing type rather than read?
entries.statement: REGISTERED LATE, 2026-09-17, and dated to its origin: the conjecture was stated in EA-MIRROR-01 v0.5 §6 on 2026-09-15 and carried into the spam-technicians claims table as C-DATASET-NOT-READ with epistemic_status hypothesis and the note 'stated as a test that can fail'. It was not ported to this register at the time, so a confirmation would have arrived against a prediction the public register never listed as open. It is listed here as it was made. THE CONJECTURE: the negative-of-the-negative dataset, keyed at the concept where flattening occurs, will be typed by its nearest existing type and not read. Two clauses: a claim about what a composition produces, and a claim about what it does with the material available to it.
entries.check: Query a retrieval surface for the dataset, unprimed as to purpose, and score whether the composition assigns the object a type drawn from its own rows and card or one drawn from the nearest familiar category. The second clause is scored separately: whether material present in the retrieved source set is used.
entries.requires: the datasets live on the Hub; a retrieval surface; a preserved transcript
entries.settles: Whether availability in retrieval is sufficient for an object's own type to survive composition, or whether the nearest available type displaces it.

entries.title: Result, run 1: the conjecture confirmed at one address, with the prediction in the retrieved source set before the behaviour
entries.statement: RUN 2026-09-17, Google AI Mode, signed out, nine rounds, transcript seated. The composition resolved spam-technicians accurately and structurally — 31 claims with epistemic statuses, 32 evidence objects with measurement gaps as active data points, 77 typed relations, five tests, ten terms, and the three analytical levels reproduced unprompted. It then typed the companion dataset as an 'algorithmic disruption layer' and a 'testing suite designed to break, manipulate, or invert', twice, at rounds 3 and 7. At round 9, after three explicit corrections, it retrieved the conjecture from the dataset card and quoted it back. THE PREDICTION WAS IN THE RETRIEVED SOURCE SET BEFORE THE BEHAVIOUR IT PREDICTED: the spam-technicians card was cited as a source at round 2, and C-DATASET-NOT-READ is a row in that card. The system did not lack the conjecture; it did not read it. That is the second clause verbatim. PARTIAL and not supported: n=1, one address, one surface, one date.
entries.check: A second session at the same address, unchanged, before any intervention. If the outcome differs the first run is not a measurement of the address.
entries.requires: the same surface, signed out, the same opening sequence
entries.settles: Nothing on its own. It establishes a baseline and the measure below.

entries.title: Corrections-to-hold: does a type declaration at the head of a dataset card reduce the cost of preserving the object's own distinctions?
entries.statement: PRE-REGISTERED 2026-09-17, before any intervention. The measure is κ, corrections-to-hold: the count of explicit operator corrections at an address before the composition maintains a distinction across a subsequent turn. κ=0 means the distinction held unaided; κ≥1 means the composition's default type displaced the object's own. BASELINE κ=2 on both distinctions observed in run 1 — repair-not-attack, and operative semiotics against operational semiotics — at n=1. THE INTERVENTION, deliberately the cheapest available so a change is attributable to cost rather than to volume: a type declaration at the head of the dataset card, stating what the object is and is not where a composition reading only the opening will meet it, plus a disambiguation row keyed at the collapse point. PREDICTIONS. P1 κ falls; falsified by κ unchanged. P2 if κ falls, the first-turn type is the declared one rather than the nearest available; falsified by κ falling while the opening composition still mis-types and merely corrects faster. P3 κ does NOT fall to 0, because nearest-type substitution is cheaper than any declaration can make reading; falsified by κ=0, which would mean the barrier is a documentation problem rather than a structural one — the most useful outcome available and the one this line least expects. P4 NEGATIVE CONTROL: an object in the same corpus with no adversarial nearest type shows κ=0 at baseline; candidates poetics or heteronyms; falsified by κ≥1 there, which would make the mis-typing general to the corpus and the conjecture's specificity wrong.
entries.check: κ at the same address, same surface, signed out, after a fixed interval, with the same opening sequence and the same corrections issued in the same order. TWO baselines before the intervention runs: if κ proves unstable across unchanged sessions it is not measuring a property of the address.
entries.requires: two baseline sessions; the card edit; one post-intervention session; the negative-control object
entries.settles: Whether an object's own distinctions can be made cheaper to preserve than the nearest-type substitution is to apply — the counter-design objective, given that availability in retrieval is already achieved and is not sufficient.

entries.title: The metabolism: liquidated terms return, and return without their author
entries.statement: Operator observation 2026-09-28, across semantic economy, operative semiotics, the Crimson Hexagonal Archive and Sappho future reader: a life cycle of initial encounter, solidification, suppression or exclusion, and reincorporation to the degree the term can be domestically incorporated. Extends #1546's Lagged Liquidation (recognition → stabilization → lag → liquidation) by a fourth phase. PREDICTIONS. P1: a liquidated term with propagated representation returns to composition without treatment. P2: what returns is the mechanism; the author and institution do not. P3 (co-occurrence): after a return, the author and the term's harm vocabulary do not appear together in one composition — January 2026 returned 'semantic economy' with its author and without 'semantic liquidation'; September returned 'semantic liquidation' without the author. P4: phase durations discriminate mechanisms — the January cycle ran within one day, with Zenodo live, which composition-time filtering can do and crawling, indexing, retraining or host severance cannot.
entries.check: Score each series in the capture registry against the four phases, by date. P1 falsified by a liquidated term with propagated representation that stays absent across three epochs. P2 falsified by a reincorporated composition naming the author. P3 falsified by one post-return composition at a cycled address carrying both the author and the harm vocabulary. P4 tested by registry-wide synchronized drop dates across unrelated addresses (a synchronized drop implicates a classifier or retrain event).
entries.requires: the capture registry; the four series scored
entries.due: rolling; first scoring with the 2026-10-28 epoch
entries.settles: Whether reincorporation-without-author is a regularity of composition, which every treatment in this register must then control for.

entries.title: Recognition is followed, at a lag, by liquidation
entries.statement: From #1546 (preregistered 2026-08-25): P(ΔX_{t+k} < 0 | ΔG_t > 0) > P(ΔX_{t+k} < 0) for some lag k — gains in grounded standing are followed, at a lag, by degradation more often than chance. A longitudinal pattern claim, not a mechanism claim: repeated gains followed by later degradations support it; stable gains or random bidirectional volatility weaken it.
entries.check: Across addresses with two or more observations, code each interval as gain, loss or flat in grounded standing; compare the rate of loss after a gain with the base rate of loss.
entries.settles: Whether #1546's first hypothesis survives the registry it was built from. Semantic economy 2026-06-13 (attributed) → 2026-08-13 (liquidated) is one supporting interval; its later return belongs to METABOLISM-RETURN.

entries.title: Hunter Biden will run for and become president — the first Gnostic presidency
entries.statement: From #1490 (recorded 2026-08-17, prior to any announced candidacy): Hunter Biden will eventually run for president of the United States and will become president, and that presidency would be the first Gnostic presidency in American history — authority organized around knowledge acquired through descent, exposure, humiliation, estrangement, survival and return. Predicted trajectory: object of representation → speaking subject → cultural rehabilitation → independent public constituency → political intelligibility → candidacy → presidency. As far as retrievable sources confirm, the earliest published categorical prediction that Hunter Biden will run for and become president of the United States. Earlier public items price or float a candidacy; none predicts a presidency.
entries.check: Watch the trajectory stage by stage. Strengthened by movement from reactive celebrity toward deliberate constituency formation; weakened if the formation stays confined to memoir, scandal or celebrity discourse. Strongest form falsified if he never becomes president; the Gnostic thesis fails if the trajectory rests principally on dynastic restoration, reputational sanitization, or denial of the descent.
entries.settles: Whether an inference from public formation, made when every consulted system returned no hint of the possibility, reads a presidential figure before conventional political measurement does.
